data.narrative:
Elementary Robotics is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $66M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including late-stage companies such as Exotec ($2.0B, Series D) and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), alongside earlier-stage peers including Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B) and Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B).

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $66M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C progression, yielding $112M. The peer-median method identifies 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B and a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B.

Triangulating these approaches produces a valuation range of $95M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $881M. The substantial spread reflects material stage and performance variation within the peer set. Key uncertainties include Elementary Robotics' revenue traction and customer concentration relative to late-stage Series D peers commanding $1.6B–$2.0B valuations, as well as differentiation relative to earlier-stage comparables. Earlier-stage positioning and limited public market data further constrain precision around the high end of this range.
